output.title: schemaguard: Types-First TS Validation
output.tagline: Runtime validators compiled from your TypeScript types — no duplicate schemas
output.description_short: Alpha library: generate runtime validators from existing TS types at build time. No Zod schema drift. 2.1 kB gzipped, ~5.5x faster than Zod.
output.description_long:
**schemaguard** is an alpha-stage TypeScript compiler plugin that generates runtime validators directly from your existing type declarations — no hand-written Zod or Yup schemas required.

**The problem it solves:** Every `interface` in a typed codebase eventually gets a duplicate schema that drifts out of sync. A production incident caused by a stale schema is the canonical trigger. schemaguard eliminates the duplicate by making your types the single source of truth.

**How it works:** A build-time plugin (esbuild or Vite) reads your TypeScript types via ts-morph and emits tiny, tree-shakeable validators. The runtime core is **2.1 kB gzipped**. In benchmarks against equivalent Zod schemas on the same payloads, schemaguard validates **~1 million objects/sec versus ~180k/sec for Zod** — roughly 5.5x throughput.

**Current state (v0.4.x):** The API is marked unstable and breaking changes occur between minor versions. Webpack support is not yet available. There is no documentation site — the README is the primary reference. Three seed-stage startups are running it in production.

**Best fit:** TypeScript-heavy teams with typed API contracts who are tired of schema drift and want validators that can never fall behind their types.
screenshot_order: 1st — side-by-side code diff: TypeScript interface on the left, zero extra schema file on the right, with a callout 'One source of truth'. This immediately shows the core value prop to a developer scanning the listing.
2nd — benchmark chart from the repo: schemaguard ~1M obj/sec vs Zod ~180k/sec on the same payload. Numbers are the strongest proof point and stop scrollers.
3rd — build output showing the 2.1 kB gzipped runtime bundle size alongside a terminal snippet of the plugin config (3-4 lines). Demonstrates low integration cost.

faq.a: It is alpha (v0.4.x). The API is unstable and breaking changes occur between minor versions. Three seed-stage startups use it in production, but evaluate carefully for critical paths.

faq.q: Do I have to rewrite my existing Zod schemas?
faq.a: No migration guide exists yet. You can adopt schemaguard incrementally at new API boundaries while keeping existing Zod schemas elsewhere.
Not yet. Webpack support is an open issue. esbuild and Vite plugins are available today.

faq.q: How does the 5.5x speed claim hold up?
faq.a: The benchmark suite is in the repo and reproducible. It compares schemaguard against an equivalent Zod schema on identical payloads — run it yourself to verify.
The runtime core is 2.1 kB gzipped. Validators are emitted at build time and tree-shakeable, so only the validators you use ship.

output.cta: Install schemaguard and validate your first API boundary in one build step

confidence.notes: All claims sourced directly from APP_PROFILE proof_points and maturity signals. Alpha status disclosed prominently. Benchmark figures are repo-reproducible per profile. Production adoption claim attributed to README statements, not independently verified.
